'''Harris Hancock''' (May 14, 1867 – March 19, 1944) was a mathematics professor at the [[University of Cincinnati]] who worked on [[algebraic number theory]] and related areas. He was the brother of the horse breeder [[Arthur B. Hancock]].

==Biography==
Harris Hancock was born at his family's estate, Ellerslie, in [[Albemarle County, Virginia]] on May 14, 1867. He graduated from the [[University of Virginia]]'s school of mathematics in 1886. He received an [[Bachelor of Arts|AB]] from [[Johns Hopkins University]] in 1888, an [[Master of Arts|AM]] and [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] from the [[University of Berlin]] in 1894, and an [[Doctor of Science|ScD]] from the [[University of Paris]] in 1901.<ref name=Cyclopaedia>{{Cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OqdgDiEkB40C&pg=PA70 |title=The National Cyclopaedia of American Biography |volume=XVI |publisher=James T. White & Company |page=70 |year=1918 |access-date=2020-12-09 |via=Google Books}}</ref>

He married Belle Lyman Clay on September 30, 1907, and they had two children.<ref name=Cyclopaedia/>

Harris Hancock died at Ellerslie on March 19, 1944.<ref>{{Cite news |url=https://www.newspapers.com/clip/64964476/educator-to-be-buried-today/ |title=Educator To Be Buried Today |newspaper=[[The Cincinnati Enquirer]] |page=11 |date=1944-03-21 |access-date=2020-12-09 |via=Newspapers.com}}</ref>
